title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 20
statement: Isosceles trapezoid \(ABCD\) has parallel sides \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{BC},\) with \(BC\lt AD\) and \(AB=CD.\) There is a point \(P\) in the plane such that \(PA=1,\) \(PB=2,\) \(PC=3,\) and \(PD=4.\) What is \(\dfrac{BC}{AD}?\)

solutions.text:
Place the trapezoid symmetric about the \(y\)-axis: \(A=(-p,0),\) \(D=(p,0),\) \(B=(-q,h),\) \(C=(q,h),\) with \(P=(x,y).\)

Then \(PA^2-PD^2=4px\) \(=1-16=-15\) and \(PB^2-PC^2=4qx\) \(=4-9=-5.\) Dividing gives \(\dfrac{p}{q}=3.\)

Since \(AD=2p\) and \(BC=2q,\) we get \(\dfrac{BC}{AD}=\dfrac{q}{p}=\dfrac13.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Both \(PA^2-PD^2\) and \(PB^2-PC^2\) equal a multiple of the \(x\)-coordinate of \(P\)
